dedupe_keys.name: bilateral trade flows of the environmental pressures of global food production producer to consumer nations

description: This data set traces food from the country that produced it to the country that ate it, and attaches the environmental cost of production to each flow. The producers are Joe DeCesaro, Gage Clawson, Haley Epperly and Melanie Frazier of the National Center for Ecological Analysis and Synthesis, Edward Allison of WorldFish, Halley Froehlich of the University of California, Santa Barbara and co-authors. Coverage is global trade in crops and animal foods from land, freshwater and ocean systems, including animal feed, with pressures for greenhouse gas emissions, water use, nitrogen and phosphorus pollution and land or water area. The authors reworked reported trade and production statistics to identify the true producing and consuming nations for each food item, which is what allows country-to-country flows to be built. The final trade matrix, full input and output data, supplementary tables and code are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: one reference period, national, not sub-national flows, and estimates inherit gaps in trade statistics. Simulation uses: building country-level food trade networks to test how export bans or production shocks propagate, and weighting flows by their environmental cost. Related records: FAOSTAT (data-faostat) and the global food shock trade model (model-global-food-shock-trade) use related trade data.
